additionalCoursework:
Humanities: Applicants should develop general cultural competence and show evidence of liberal arts exploration. The Humanities Competencies will typically be satisfied through 6 semester hours of college coursework in the arts, humanities, social sciences or language. Some fluency in a foreign language is encouraged, but not required.

Writing & Analysis: Applicants should be able to analyze sources of evidence, develop a thesis, and support an argument logically with appropriate attribution.
The Writing & Analysis Competencies will typically be satisfied through one year of coursework emphasizing writing and analysis, which may be in applied or basic sciences or humanities. Where appropriate, writing coursework may also satisfy the Humanities competencies.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
All Pritzker students are supported by a broad network of faculty and staff. The Office of Student Affairs and Programs and the Office of Health Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion are two of the many entry points for students to access important services and information.

The Office of Student Affairs and Programs offers valuable resources for career development and mentorship, as well as personal and professional well-being. In addition to our formal programs, you will find that informal mentoring relationships develop through regular interactions with faculty, staff, and classmates.

The Office of Health Equity, Diversity, and Inclusion works with all offices at Pritzker to create an inclusive learning environment to support students in their professional growth, scholarly pursuits, and community-engaged activities.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: The Associate Dean for Medical School Education and Career Advisers work closely with students as they move through the UChicago Pritzker curriculum. The flexibility is available for students to take a leave of absence for personal reasons or to pursue combined degrees, to decompress their courseload, to engage in a time of research or other scholarly activity.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: UChicago Pritzker is home to more than 50 student organizations, including programs for community outreach, tutoring, special interest groups, and recreational clubs. From free medical-student-run clinics to teaching students through South Side Science Scholars, our students take an active interest in both the community surrounding them and society on a global scale. Other activities range from intramural sports to the Pritzker Book Club.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: The University of Chicago is located on the south side of Chicago in the diverse community of Hyde Park, just minutes by train or bus from downtown Chicago. The medical school and hospital system are all located on the University's main Hyde Park campus, while the resources of our world-class city and its extraordinary lakefront are at the campus doorstep. UChicago Medicine, with over 20 buildings and 22 acres of space for research, teaching, and patient care, is within easy walking distance of UChicago Pritzker's libraries, classrooms, and labs. The medical campus includes the ten-story Center for Care and Discovery, which provides a home for complex specialty care. The much-anticipated adult trauma center opened for patient care in 2018. Students are able to participate in interdisciplinary opportunities across campus, including taking courses in other departments as early as the first year of medical school.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
All medical students reside in off-campus housing. As a part of an extensive admitted student and orientation program, students are guided in their housing search. In a typical year, over 90% of first-year students live in the Hyde Park neighborhood.

The University also offers a variety of free transportation options including buses, shuttles, and a RideSmart program for late evening/early morning transportation to and from campus. The majority of our students do not bring a car to medical school and rely on Chicago's world-class public transportation to provide easy access to the city.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: OUTPatient, the LGBTQ+ people in medicine group and a chapter of the Medical Student Pride Alliance, provides a supportive, social forum for both LGBTQ students and allies. OUTPatient also offers education to the Pritzker community on LGBTQ related topics. In 2023, OUTPatient received an honorable mention for the Medical Student Pride Alliance's Chapter of the Year Award. The University of Chicago's Center for Identity + Inclusion also offers extensive resources for students.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
The Pritzker School of Medicine embraces wellness as a core value and is committed to helping students thrive in medical school through tailored programming to enhance physical, emotional, social, and spiritual well-being.  

Pritzker invests in a wealth of resources dedicated to student support and wellness throughout their medical school experience. The Pritzker Wellness Program equips students with life-long skills to enhance their health and well-being by creating a culture that promotes reflection, compassion and the pursuit of joy on their path to personal and professional growth. 

https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/student-life/psom-student-support-and-wellness
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
Our small class size (90 per class) leads to a tight-knit community with personalized mentorship and support for each individual student. Each student is also a member of a Pritzker Society which provide career advising of medical students from medical school entry through Match Day and graduation. The societies are vertically integrated to enhance collegial and collaborative opportunities and to foster mentoring, both faculty to student, and more experienced students to newer students. 

A 2024 Pritzker alumnus shared: "Pritzker exemplified everything I valued most in medical education. The emphasis on prioritizing under-resourced communities, the culture of collaboration & growth, the supportive faculty, and student engagement was truly unmatched by any other school. The day I got my acceptance I was speechless. I knew in the back of my mind that no other school was going to give me the love and support Pritzker would."
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: The University of Chicago provides robust transportation resources for students, including free bus and shuttle routes both on campus and throughout the Hyde Park neighborhood, in addition to RideSmart, UChicago’s exclusive on-demand rideshare program. Chicago's outstanding public transit system allows students to navigate the greater city with ease.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Business casual/business professional in the clinical settings.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Students receive academic support from faculty course directors, the Associate Dean for Medical Student Academic Advising and Advancement, a full-time learning specialist, and peer educators.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students are immersed in the clinical environment during the first week of medical school. M1 students participate in Clinical Skills courses and Ambulatory and Inpatient Mentoring throughout Phase 1.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Student-centered, with an appreciation of the diverse learning styles that students bring to Pritzker.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: During Phase 2 of our three-phase curriculum, which begins 1.5 years in to medical school.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The Pritzker Phoenix Curriculum, established in 2023, includes an emphasis on active learning, robust clinical skills education, integration among disciplines, a focus on health equity and advocacy, and a requirement for a scholarly project for all medical students.

The Phoenix Curriculum consists of three phases: 

- Phase 1: Scientific Foundations and Physician Formation
- Phase 2: Core Clinical Clerkships
- Phase 3: Differentiation and Transition

During Phase 1 ( https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/academics/phase-one-courses ), students take anatomy, basic science courses, Health Equity, Advocacy, and Anti-Racism, health policy, ethics, and complete robust clinical skills coursework along with our Ambulatory and Inpatient Mentoring program which places students in clinical settings early in medical school. The Phase 2 core clerkships ( https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/academics/phase-2-core-clerkships ) begin midway through the second year. During Phase 3 (https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/academics/phoenix-phase-3), students tailor their curriculum to their intended specialty and are prepared for the transition to residency. 

To further promote an atmosphere of shared learning and collaboration, the Pritzker curriculum uses a Pass/Fail grading system. The Pass/Fail system encourages cooperation among students, develops lifelong learners, and allows students to prioritize their learning and extracurricular experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: UChicago is committed to providing excellent primary care to the vulnerable and underserved populations in our surrounding communities on the South Side of Chicago. Our hospital system, UChicago Medicine, has also been the home of innovations like the Comprehensive Care Program, created to revitalize the primary care doctor–patient relationship and to offer Medicare patients with complex medical and social needs a comprehensive care physician who cares for them in both the hospital and the clinic.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: The University of Chicago is one of the preeminent academic medical centers in the world and offers students an abundance of interdisciplinary opportunities to explore and discover. Students have the opportunity to contribute to the production of new knowledge through their own research, guided by faculty who are outstanding teachers, invested mentors, and leading scientists. The NIH-funded Summer Research Program is an 11-week research opportunity providing stipend support to medical students in the summer following the first year. All MD students participate in a mentored scholarly project through our Scholarship & Discovery tracks with protected curricular time ( https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/academics/scholarship-discovery ).
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: There are a multitude of opportunities for students to engage in community service through our six student-run free clinics, educational programs, and other community partnerships.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: 100% of students complete a scholarly project through our Scholarship & Discovery program for MD students or a PhD program: https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/academics/scholarship-discovery
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: Clinical training occurs primarily at our affiliated hospital system, UChicago Medicine, which attracts patients from the surrounding Chicago metropolitan area and throughout the world.

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation:
The University of Chicago Pritzker School of Medicine offers medical students opportunities for interdisciplinary learning, outstanding clinical training, and innovative research, all alongside an abiding commitment to health equity. We are enriched by and invested in the community we call home: the South Side of Chicago, and students engage in longitudinal community partnerships through a variety of educational and health organizations, including six student-run free clinics.

Research opportunities also abound at UChicago, and Pritzker consistently ranks as one of the top institutions for NIH research grants per faculty member. Students pursue mentored scholarly work through our Scholarship & Discovery program (which provides protected time and funding throughout the curriculum) or one of three MD/PhD programs. 

As a small medical school, students also receive individual mentorship and support through programs like the Pritzker career advising societies and Pritzker Wellness.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
At the University of Chicago, in an atmosphere of interdisciplinary scholarship and discovery, the Pritzker School of Medicine is dedicated to inspiring diverse students of exceptional promise to become leaders and innovators in science and medicine for the betterment of humanity.

---

Our mission statement is an expression of our core purpose and educational philosophy. In particular, it highlights the value we place on service, leadership, and the creation of new knowledge. These values guide both our admissions process and the education that Pritzker students receive.

We view our students as future leaders who will make an impact in healthcare and science and are committed to ensuring that our students are well-positioned to successfully pursue the next phase of their training and careers. Our Phoenix Curriculum emphasizes the relationship between the basic/clinical sciences and community/population health while providing students with ample time for self-directed learning, research, community engagement, and training in health equity and medical ethics, while accelerating entry into the clinical clerkships. 
 
During phase two of the curriculum, Pritzker students complete the majority of their clinical training at UChicago Medicine (UCM), the only tertiary care center on the South Side of Chicago. UCM, nationally recognized by the AAMC for sustained commitment to community engagement, partnership, and collaboration, has a primary service area where poverty is over double the state level. Additionally, our students lead numerous community-based initiatives throughout Chicago, including six free clinics that primarily serve uninsured patients.Our Admissions Committee values applicants whose personal mission within medicine includes health justice, equitable delivery of healthcare, and service to underserved and marginalized communities. Our students carry this mission beyond their medical school years, and the majority of our students plan to care primarily for underserved populations during their careers in medicine (2025 AAMC Graduation Questionnaire).

Our students are also deeply invested in scholarship and discovery, with access to world-renowned, interdisciplinary faculty mentors and experts in basic/translational science, health services/data science, community health, global health, medical education, and clinical research. 100% of our students complete a mentored research project, and faculty and students are supported in scholarship and discovery through focused, funded, and longitudinal research experiences embedded within the core curriculum. 
 
At the Pritzker School of Medicine, medical students are valued members of our community. Our robust advising and mentorship structure, commitment to student wellbeing and vitality, and atmosphere of collaboration, support, and excellence ensure that the Pritzker medical student is poised to help shape the future of medicine.

medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
One committee letter or premedical advisor letter will fulfill the requirement. Three individual letters will also fulfill the requirement. We will accept a maximum of five individual letters. 

If a pre-medical committee letter does not include individual supporting letters, we recommend submitting those alongside the committee letter/evaluation.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: A minimum of two science faculty letters is strongly recommended.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay: Applicants will have three one-on-one interviews with a faculty member, a student, and a Pritzker administrator, along with informational sessions with faculty, staff, and current students.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: Three one-on-one interviews via Zoom with a faculty, administrator, and medical student.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: All interviews will be via video for the 2026-27 cycle.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: N/A - tuition is the same for in- and out-of-state students
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: As a private institution, there is no difference in our evaluation or preference for in- and out-of-state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: We accept applications from Canadian applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptInternationalApplInformation: We accept applications from international applicants.
medSchoolApplication.dacaDetail: We accept applications from DACA applicants.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo: Application policies and information are available on our website at https://pritzker.uchicago.edu/admissions/admissions-process
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our Admissions Committee views all lifetime MCAT scores.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: While we do not have required minimum MCAT score for consideration, we strongly encourage applicants to view our MCAT data in the MSAR.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: While we do not have required minimum GPA for consideration, we strongly encourage applicants to view our MCAT data in the MSAR.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: We do not have required minimum GPAs for screening. All components of the GPA are considered, as well as any trends over time.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: All postbaccalaureate and graduate coursework (regardless of number of hours taken) will be reviewed and considered by the admissions committee, along with the applicant's undergraduate GPA.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: Prerequisites taken at a community college can be used to demonstrate our required competencies. If you take prerequisite courses at a community college, we do recommend taking rigorous, upper-level science courses at a four-year institution as well.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Our committee welcomes communication from applicants at any stage of the process. Application updates and letters of intent or interest may be submitted at any time: pre-interview, post-interview, or during the waitlist process.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Information about our Technical Standards is included on our website linked below.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
UChicago Pritzker provides a comprehensive financial aid program that is deeply committed to helping students manage their educational costs both during and after medical school. The Financial Aid Office offers individual debt management counseling to all incoming students, provides consultations throughout the four years, and offers an AAMC loan repayment strategy session for all graduating students.

Each year, UChicago offers significant scholarship support to incoming students, with half of incoming students receiving full tuition scholarships. Additional institutional resources are provided through low-interest University of Chicago loans. International and DACA applications are eligible for scholarships and University of Chicago loans, while U.S. citizens and permanent residents may receive federal loans.

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: A subset of interviewed students who are not originally accepted are invited to join our waitlist. Our waitlist is unranked.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Our competency based requirements emphasize not the number of courses taken, but the level of mastery that should be achieved. Since the emphasis is on competencies, in some cases an applicant may satisfy the required competency with fewer courses.

Information on our required competencies can be found on our website.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: No formal expiration date, but course completion date is considered as academic preparation is evaluated.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Offers of admission are made based on a thorough review of the entire admissions file, letters of recommendation, and interviews. Outstanding personal characteristics, strong evidence of commitment to a career in medicine, and alignment with our program's mission statement are as important as excellence in academics. We strongly encourage applicants to review our website, mission statement, and information included above and to consider how their own personal mission aligns with our program.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: While we do not have a required number of shadowing experiences or a minimum hour requirement, evidence of exploration of a career in medicine through clinical volunteering, paid clinical experiences, shadowing, and/or other clinical experiences are important in our admissions committee's evaluations.
